text.p: Nasdaq stocks rallied to a new record close on Monday, drawing strength mostly from semis and circumventing weakness in some stocks including the disaster of the day -- Westell Technologies Inc.
The Nasdaq Composite Index was up 3.22 points, or 0.26 percent, at 1250.78 at its unofficial close while declines led advancing issues by 2204 to 1884 on volume of about 484 million shares.
The previous record was set on June 5 when the Composite closed at 1259.15.
"The semiconductors are leading the charge. But I see a lot of red on my screen too," said Brett Discher, vice president of equity trading at Dain Bosworth.
But while stocks Intel Corp was up 2-115/16 at 104-5/8 and Microsoft Corp was up 1-1/8 at 137-1/2, the day also had its share of disappointments.

Westell Technologies was down 12-3/8 at 34 after the company said it was disappointed it was not awarded an initial contract to supply modems to a consortium of regional Bell operators, but expects to be an important vendor to the companies in the future.
